title: Investigating an Outbound Traffic Alert
context: A workstation is sending data to an unknown external IP on an unusual port. You must preserve evidence and reconstruct the facts in three decisions.

n1.text: The host is still active. What is the first action?

choices.text: Capture memory and active connections before any isolation or shutdown
choices.why: RAM and connections are the most volatile evidence: isolating or shutting down too quickly destroys them.

choices.text: Immediately power off the workstation to stop exfiltration
choices.why: Powering off erases keys, processes, and connections needed for the investigation.

choices.text: Reboot the workstation to get a clean state
choices.why: Rebooting destroys memory: it is the classic mistake.

n2.text: Which source will tell you which process initiated this connection?

choices.text: Endpoint logs cross-referenced with the memory capture and active connections
choices.why: The offending process often lives in memory and has no file on disk (fileless).
The dashboard guides analysis, but does not identify the process.
The firewall sees the destination, not the local process that issued the request.

n3.text: You must share the artifacts with stakeholders. How do you proceed?

choices.text: Hash each artifact, document chain of custody, restrict access, and involve HR/Legal if needed
choices.why: Integrity, traceability, and legal framework make evidence usable.

choices.text: Email the capture to the entire team
choices.why: This breaks the chain of custody and exposes potentially sensitive data.

choices.text: Post the artifacts on an open channel
choices.why: Publicly disclosed evidence is no longer reliable or admissible.

n4.outcome: You preserved volatile evidence, identified the process through correlation, and maintained the evidentiary value of the artifacts.

debrief: Order of volatility takes precedence over the temptation to power off or reboot.
Cross-referencing endpoint + memory + network reveals what a single source cannot.
Hashing, chain of custody, and HR/Legal involvement govern how evidence can be used.
